chapters.title: The Count of Israel
chapters.html:
Numbers 1

1The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tent of meeting, on the first of the second month, in the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt, saying,

2"Take a count of the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, by the number of names, every male, head by head,

3from twenty years old and up, all in Israel who can go out to war. You and Aaron shall count them by their divisions.

4With you there shall be a man from each tribe, each one the head of his fathers' house.

5These are the names of the men who shall stand with you: from Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur;

6from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;

7from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab;

8from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar;

9from Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon;

10from the sons of Joseph: from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud; from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;

11from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni;

12from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;

13from Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran;

14from Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel;

15from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan."

16These were the ones called from the congregation, the chiefs of their fathers' tribes. They were the heads of the thousands of Israel.

17Moses and Aaron took these men who had been designated by name,

18and they assembled the whole congregation on the first of the second month, and they registered their descent by their clans, by their fathers' houses, by the number of names, from twenty years old and up, head by head,

19as the LORD had commanded Moses. He counted them in the wilderness of Sinai.

The Count by Tribes

20The sons of Reuben, Israel's firstborn — their descendants, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, by the number of names, head by head, every male twenty years old and up, all who could go out to war:

21those of them counted, of the tribe of Reuben, were forty-six thousand five hundred.

22Of the sons of Simeon — their descendants, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, those of them counted, by the number of names, head by head, every male twenty years old and up, all who could go out to war:

23those of them counted, of the tribe of Simeon, were fifty-nine thousand three hundred.

24Of the sons of Gad — their descendants, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, by the number of names, twenty years old and up, all who could go out to war:

25those of them counted, of the tribe of Gad, were forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.

26Of the sons of Judah — their descendants, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, by the number of names, twenty years old and up, all who could go out to war:

27those of them counted, of the tribe of Judah, were seventy-four thousand six hundred.

28Of the sons of Issachar — their descendants, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, by the number of names, twenty years old and up, all who could go out to war:

29those of them counted, of the tribe of Issachar, were fifty-four thousand four hundred.

30Of the sons of Zebulun — their descendants, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, by the number of names, twenty years old and up, all who could go out to war:

31those of them counted, of the tribe of Zebulun, were fifty-seven thousand four hundred.

32Of the sons of Joseph: of the sons of Ephraim — their descendants, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, by the number of names, twenty years old and up, all who could go out to war:

33those of them counted, of the tribe of Ephraim, were forty thousand five hundred.

34Of the sons of Manasseh — their descendants, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, by the number of names, twenty years old and up, all who could go out to war:

35those of them counted, of the tribe of Manasseh, were thirty-two thousand two hundred.

36Of the sons of Benjamin — their descendants, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, by the number of names, twenty years old and up, all who could go out to war:

37those of them counted, of the tribe of Benjamin, were thirty-five thousand four hundred.

38Of the sons of Dan — their descendants, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, by the number of names, twenty years old and up, all who could go out to war:

39those of them counted, of the tribe of Dan, were sixty-two thousand seven hundred.

40Of the sons of Asher — their descendants, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, by the number of names, twenty years old and up, all who could go out to war:

41those of them counted, of the tribe of Asher, were forty-one thousand five hundred.

42Of the sons of Naphtali — their descendants, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, by the number of names, twenty years old and up, all who could go out to war:

43those of them counted, of the tribe of Naphtali, were fifty-three thousand four hundred.

44These are the ones counted, whom Moses and Aaron counted with the chiefs of Israel, twelve men, each one for his fathers' house.

45All those counted of the sons of Israel, by their fathers' houses, from twenty years old and up, all in Israel who could go out to war —

46all those counted were six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.

The Levites

47But the Levites were not counted among them by their fathers' tribe.

48For the LORD had spoken to Moses, saying,

49"Only the tribe of Levi you shall not count, and you shall not take a count of them among the sons of Israel.

50But you — appoint the Levites over the dwelling of the Testimony, and over all its vessels, and over everything that belongs to it. They shall carry the dwelling and all its vessels, and they shall serve it, and they shall camp around the dwelling.

51When the dwelling sets out, the Levites shall take it down, and when the dwelling camps, the Levites shall set it up. The outsider who comes near shall be put to death.

52The sons of Israel shall camp each in his own camp and each by his own banner, by their divisions.

53But the Levites shall camp around the dwelling of the Testimony, so that there will be no wrath on the congregation of the sons of Israel. The Levites shall keep the charge of the dwelling of the Testimony."

54The sons of Israel did so. According to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so they did.

Notes

  • v1 "in the wilderness" — be-midbar, the Hebrew name of this book, taken from its first line. The English name Numbers comes through Latin from the Greek Arithmoi, named for the two counts of the people (chapters 1 and 26). The date is exact: one month after the dwelling was raised on the first of the first month (Exodus 40:17). Israel has been at Sinai nearly a year.

  • v2 "take a count" — se'u et rosh, literally lift the head. It is the idiom of Joseph's two dreams in prison: Pharaoh will lift your head and restore you, the cupbearer is told, and the baker, lift your head from off you (Genesis 40:13, 19). Head by head is le-gulgelotam, by their skulls, the word behind Golgotha.

  • v3 "all who can go out to war" — kol yotse tsava, everyone who goes out with the army. The count is a muster. The verb, paqad, is to count and also to attend to, to take charge of, and to visit. The count is God taking stock of what He brought out of Egypt.

  • v16 "the heads of the thousands of Israel" — elef means a thousand, and it also means a clan, a family unit: my clan is the weakest in Manasseh, Gideon says (Judges 6:15), using this word. The census totals in this chapter are written with elef. Read as thousands, the fighting men number 603,550, the same figure as the half-shekel count in Exodus 38:26. Read as clans or units, the numbers would be far smaller. Both senses of the word are real; the totals the text itself adds up (v46) follow the thousand reading.

  • v17 "designated by name" — nikkevu, from naqav, the verb used of the man who blasphemed the Name in Leviticus 24:11. The same verb that marks a name out for honor here marks it out for abuse there.

  • v18 "registered their descent" — va-yityaldu, a form of yalad, to give birth, that occurs here and nowhere else: they had themselves born, each one stating whose son he was. The count of an army is also a roll of ancestry.

  • v20 "Reuben, Israel's firstborn" — the list opens with the firstborn, as Genesis 49 did, and names Joseph's two sons as tribes (vv32–35), as Jacob did when he adopted them (Genesis 48:5). Levi is missing from the twelve; Ephraim and Manasseh keep the count at twelve.

  • vv47–53 the Levites are not counted — the tribe that carries the dwelling is not mustered for war. It camps around the dwelling as a living wall, so that there will be no wrath on the congregation: the Levites stand between the people and the holy place.

chapters.title: The Camp Around the Tent
chapters.html:
Numbers 2

1The LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

2"The sons of Israel shall camp each by his own banner, under the signs of their fathers' houses. They shall camp facing the tent of meeting, at a distance, all around it.

East: Judah

3Those camping on the east side, toward the sunrise, shall be the banner of the camp of Judah by their divisions. The chief of the sons of Judah is Nahshon son of Amminadab,

4and his army, those of them counted, seventy-four thousand six hundred.

5Those camping next to him shall be the tribe of Issachar. The chief of the sons of Issachar is Nethanel son of Zuar,

6and his army, those of it counted, fifty-four thousand four hundred.

7Then the tribe of Zebulun. The chief of the sons of Zebulun is Eliab son of Helon,

8and his army, those of it counted, fifty-seven thousand four hundred.

9All those counted for the camp of Judah, by their divisions, one hundred and eighty-six thousand four hundred. They shall set out first.

South: Reuben

10The banner of the camp of Reuben shall be on the south, by their divisions. The chief of the sons of Reuben is Elizur son of Shedeur,

11and his army, those of it counted, forty-six thousand five hundred.

12Those camping next to him shall be the tribe of Simeon. The chief of the sons of Simeon is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai,

13and his army, those of them counted, fifty-nine thousand three hundred.

14Then the tribe of Gad. The chief of the sons of Gad is Eliasaph son of Reuel,

15and his army, those of them counted, forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.

16All those counted for the camp of Reuben, by their divisions, one hundred and fifty-one thousand four hundred and fifty. They shall set out second.

The Tent in the Middle

17The tent of meeting shall set out, the camp of the Levites, in the middle of the camps. As they camp, so they shall set out, each in his place, by their banners.

West: Ephraim

18The banner of the camp of Ephraim shall be on the west, by their divisions. The chief of the sons of Ephraim is Elishama son of Ammihud,

19and his army, those of them counted, forty thousand five hundred.

20Next to him the tribe of Manasseh. The chief of the sons of Manasseh is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur,

21and his army, those of them counted, thirty-two thousand two hundred.

22Then the tribe of Benjamin. The chief of the sons of Benjamin is Abidan son of Gideoni,

23and his army, those of them counted, thirty-five thousand four hundred.

24All those counted for the camp of Ephraim, by their divisions, one hundred and eight thousand one hundred. They shall set out third.

North: Dan

25The banner of the camp of Dan shall be on the north, by their divisions. The chief of the sons of Dan is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai,

26and his army, those of them counted, sixty-two thousand seven hundred.

27Those camping next to him shall be the tribe of Asher. The chief of the sons of Asher is Pagiel son of Ocran,

28and his army, those of them counted, forty-one thousand five hundred.

29Then the tribe of Naphtali. The chief of the sons of Naphtali is Ahira son of Enan,

30and his army, those of them counted, fifty-three thousand four hundred.

31All those counted for the camp of Dan, one hundred and fifty-seven thousand six hundred. They shall set out last, by their banners."

32These are those of the sons of Israel counted by their fathers' houses. All those counted in the camps, by their divisions, were six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.

33But the Levites were not counted among the sons of Israel, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

34The sons of Israel did according to all that the LORD had commanded Moses. So they camped by their banners, and so they set out, each by his clans, by his fathers' house.

Notes

  • v2 "facing the tent of meeting, at a distance" — mi-neged saviv, opposite and all around. Every tent in Israel faces the dwelling, and none comes close. Four camps of three tribes make a square, the Levites form an inner ring (1:53), and the tent of meeting stands in the middle (v17). When the camp moves, it keeps the same shape.

  • v3 "on the east side, toward the sunrise" — qedmah mizrachah. The entrance to the court of the dwelling faces the sunrise (Exodus 27:13), and Judah camps in front of it and marches first. The largest tribe holds the door. East is also where the way back into Eden was guarded (Genesis 3:24).

  • v10, 18, 25 the four directions — Hebrew names them by where a person stands facing the sunrise: qedem, east, is also before, in front; teiman, south, is from yamin, the right hand; the west is yam, the sea; the north, tsafon, is from a root meaning hidden. The camp is laid out as a man facing east would see the world.

  • v14 "Eliasaph son of Reuel" — in 1:14 and three more times (7:42, 7:47, 10:20) his father is Deuel. The Hebrew letters d and r are nearly the same shape, and one of the two spellings is a copyist's slip. The Greek has Reuel in every place. The text stands as the Hebrew has it in each verse.

  • v17 "as they camp, so they shall set out" — the tent of meeting marches in the middle, with two camps ahead of it and two behind. The order of the march is the order of the camp, and God's dwelling is at the center of both.

  • v32 "six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty" — the total of chapter 1, now broken into four camps of 186,400, 151,450, 108,100 and 157,600. The four add up exactly. On thousand and clan, see the note on 1:16.

chapters.title: The Levites in Place of the Firstborn
chapters.html:
Numbers 3

The Sons of Aaron

1These are the begettings of Aaron and Moses, on the day the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.

2These are the names of the sons of Aaron: the firstborn Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

3These are the names of the sons of Aaron, the anointed priests, whose hand he filled to serve as priests.

4Nadab and Abihu died before the LORD when they brought strange fire near before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no sons. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests in the presence of Aaron their father.

The Levites Given to Aaron

5The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

6"Bring the tribe of Levi near, and set it before Aaron the priest, and they shall serve him.

7They shall keep his charge and the charge of the whole congregation before the tent of meeting, doing the work of the dwelling.

8They shall keep all the vessels of the tent of meeting, and the charge of the sons of Israel, doing the work of the dwelling.

9You shall give the Levites to Aaron and to his sons. Wholly given they are to him, from the sons of Israel.

10You shall appoint Aaron and his sons, and they shall keep their priesthood. The outsider who comes near shall be put to death."

11The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

12"I — here, I have taken the Levites from among the sons of Israel in place of every firstborn, every opener of the womb among the sons of Israel. The Levites shall be Mine.

13For every firstborn is Mine. On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I set apart for Myself every firstborn in Israel, from man to beast. They shall be Mine. I am the LORD."

The Count of the Levites

14The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying,

15"Count the sons of Levi by their fathers' houses, by their clans. Every male from a month old and upward you shall count."

16Moses counted them at the word of the LORD, as he had been commanded.

17These were the sons of Levi by their names: Gershon and Kohath and Merari.

18These are the names of the sons of Gershon by their clans: Libni and Shimei.

19The sons of Kohath by their clans: Amram and Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.

20The sons of Merari by their clans: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites by their fathers' houses.

Gershon: West

21To Gershon belonged the clan of the Libnites and the clan of the Shimeites. These are the clans of the Gershonites.

22Those of them counted, by the number of every male from a month old and upward — those of them counted were seven thousand five hundred.

23The clans of the Gershonites shall camp behind the dwelling, on the west.

24The chief of the fathers' house of the Gershonites is Eliasaph son of Lael.

25The charge of the sons of Gershon in the tent of meeting is the dwelling and the tent, its covering, and the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting,

26and the hangings of the court, and the screen for the entrance of the court that is around the dwelling and the altar, and its cords — all the work of it.

Kohath: South

27To Kohath belonged the clan of the Amramites and the clan of the Izharites and the clan of the Hebronites and the clan of the Uzzielites. These are the clans of the Kohathites.

28By the number of every male from a month old and upward, eight thousand six hundred, keeping the charge of the holy place.

29The clans of the sons of Kohath shall camp on the side of the dwelling, on the south.

30The chief of the fathers' house of the clans of the Kohathites is Elizaphan son of Uzziel.

31Their charge is the ark and the table and the lampstand and the altars, and the vessels of the holy place with which they serve, and the screen — all the work of it.

32The chief over the chiefs of the Levites is Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, with oversight of those who keep the charge of the holy place.

Merari: North

33To Merari belonged the clan of the Mahlites and the clan of the Mushites. These are the clans of Merari.

34Those of them counted, by the number of every male from a month old and upward, were six thousand two hundred.

35The chief of the fathers' house of the clans of Merari is Zuriel son of Abihail. They shall camp on the side of the dwelling, on the north.

36The appointed charge of the sons of Merari is the frames of the dwelling and its bars and its pillars and its sockets and all its equipment — all the work of it —

37and the pillars of the court all around, and their sockets and their pegs and their cords.

Moses and Aaron: East

38Those camping before the dwelling on the east, before the tent of meeting toward the sunrise, are Moses and Aaron and his sons, keeping the charge of the sanctuary, the charge for the sons of Israel. The outsider who comes near shall be put to death.

39All those counted of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the word of the LORD by their clans, every male from a month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand.

The Firstborn Redeemed

40The LORD said to Moses, "Count every firstborn male of the sons of Israel from a month old and upward, and take the number of their names.

41You shall take the Levites for Me — I am the LORD — in place of every firstborn among the sons of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites in place of every firstborn among the livestock of the sons of Israel."

42Moses counted, as the LORD had commanded him, every firstborn among the sons of Israel.

43All the firstborn males, by the number of names, from a month old and upward, of those counted, were twenty-two thousand two hundred and seventy-three.

44The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

45"Take the Levites in place of every firstborn among the sons of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites shall be Mine. I am the LORD.

46For the redemption of the two hundred and seventy-three of the firstborn of the sons of Israel who are more than the Levites,

47you shall take five shekels apiece, head by head. By the shekel of the sanctuary you shall take it; twenty gerahs make a shekel.

48You shall give the money to Aaron and to his sons, the redemption of those who are more than their number."

49Moses took the redemption money from those who were more than the ones redeemed by the Levites.

50From the firstborn of the sons of Israel he took the money, one thousand three hundred and sixty-five shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary.

51Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and to his sons at the word of the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

Notes

  • v1 "the begettings of Aaron and Moses" — toledot, the word that divides Genesis into its families: these are the begettings of the heavens and the earth (Genesis 2:4), of Noah (6:9), of Terah (11:27), of Jacob (37:2). This is the only time the formula appears in the rest of the five books. Then it names Aaron's sons and no one else. Moses's sons are never listed with the priests; 1 Chronicles 23:14 says of them, the sons of Moses the man of God were named among the tribe of Levi. The family line of Moses, in the sense that matters here, is the priesthood of his brother.

  • v3 "whose hand he filled" — mille yadam, the idiom for ordaining a priest (Leviticus 8:33). At their ordination Moses put the portions of the offering into their hands (8:27).

  • v4 "in the presence of Aaron their father" — al penei, literally on the face of. It can mean in his sight or during his lifetime, as when Haran died before the face of Terah his father (Genesis 11:28), while his father still lived. Both are true here: the two younger sons took up the work while their father was still the high priest, in front of him.

  • v9 "wholly given" — netunim netunim, given, given: the word doubled for completeness. Here the Levites are given to him, to Aaron. At their dedication the same doubled word is used, but God says they are given, given to Me (8:16), and the Greek already reads to Me in this verse. They belong to God, and He hands them to the priests.

  • vv12–13 "in place of every firstborn" — the firstborn were claimed on the night Egypt's firstborn died: set apart to Me every firstborn (Exodus 13:2). Now one tribe stands in for all of them, and the firstborn of every other tribe go back to their families.

  • v38 "the outsider who comes near shall be put to death" — ha-zar, the word for anyone not entitled to the holy things (Leviticus 22:10). Moses and Aaron camp in front of the only entrance, on the east. Anyone entering has to pass them.

  • vv22, 28, 34, 39 the Levite total — the three clans add up to 7,500 + 8,600 + 6,200 = 22,300, but v39 says 22,000. The Greek does not reconcile it: it has 6,050 for Merari, which makes 22,150. The 22,000 is the number the rest of the chapter uses, set against 22,273 firstborn to leave 273 over (v46). The Hebrew words for six (shesh) and three (shalosh) differ by one letter, so v28 may once have read 8,300, which would make the sum exact. No witness here has that reading.

  • v39 "and Aaron" — in the Hebrew text the word ve-Aharon has a dot written over every letter. It is one of ten places in the five books where the scribes marked a word this way (Genesis 33:4 is another). The dots flag the word as questioned. Aaron is not named in the command to count (v15) or in the count itself (v16), so the dots may mark his name as added.

  • v47 "five shekels apiece, head by head" — la-gulgolet, by the skull, the word of the census in 1:2. The firstborn left over after each Levite stands for one of them are bought back at five shekels each, the price set for a boy from a month to five years old in the valuations of Leviticus 27:6. 273 × 5 = 1,365 (v50).

speech.text: Numbers 3
The Sons of Aaron
These are the begettings of Aaron and Moses, on the day the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
These are the names of the sons of Aaron: the firstborn Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
These are the names of the sons of Aaron, the anointed priests, whose hand he filled to serve as priests.

Nadab and Abihu died before the LORD when they brought strange fire near before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no sons. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests in the presence of Aaron their father.
The Levites Given to Aaron
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Bring the tribe of Levi near, and set it before Aaron the priest, and they shall serve him.
They shall keep his charge and the charge of the whole congregation before the tent of meeting, doing the work of the dwelling.
They shall keep all the vessels of the tent of meeting, and the charge of the sons of Israel, doing the work of the dwelling.
You shall give the Levites to Aaron and to his sons. Wholly given they are to him, from the sons of Israel.
You shall appoint Aaron and his sons, and they shall keep their priesthood. The outsider who comes near shall be put to death."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"I — here, I have taken the Levites from among the sons of Israel in place of every firstborn, every opener of the womb among the sons of Israel. The Levites shall be Mine.
For every firstborn is Mine. On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I set apart for Myself every firstborn in Israel, from man to beast. They shall be Mine. I am the LORD."
The Count of the Levites
The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying,
"Count the sons of Levi by their fathers' houses, by their clans. Every male from a month old and upward you shall count."
Moses counted them at the word of the LORD, as he had been commanded.
These were the sons of Levi by their names: Gershon and Kohath and Merari.
These are the names of the sons of Gershon by their clans: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath by their clans: Amram and Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari by their clans: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites by their fathers' houses.
Gershon: West
To Gershon belonged the clan of the Libnites and the clan of the Shimeites. These are the clans of the Gershonites.
Those of them counted, by the number of every male from a month old and upward — those of them counted were seven thousand five hundred.
The clans of the Gershonites shall camp behind the dwelling, on the west.
The chief of the fathers' house of the Gershonites is Eliasaph son of Lael.
The charge of the sons of Gershon in the tent of meeting is the dwelling and the tent, its covering, and the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting,
and the hangings of the court, and the screen for the entrance of the court that is around the dwelling and the altar, and its cords — all the work of it.
Kohath: South
To Kohath belonged the clan of the Amramites and the clan of the Izharites and the clan of the Hebronites and the clan of the Uzzielites. These are the clans of the Kohathites.
By the number of every male from a month old and upward, eight thousand six hundred, keeping the charge of the holy place.
The clans of the sons of Kohath shall camp on the side of the dwelling, on the south.
The chief of the fathers' house of the clans of the Kohathites is Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
Their charge is the ark and the table and the lampstand and the altars, and the vessels of the holy place with which they serve, and the screen — all the work of it.
The chief over the chiefs of the Levites is Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, with oversight of those who keep the charge of the holy place.
Merari: North
To Merari belonged the clan of the Mahlites and the clan of the Mushites. These are the clans of Merari.
Those of them counted, by the number of every male from a month old and upward, were six thousand two hundred.
The chief of the fathers' house of the clans of Merari is Zuriel son of Abihail. They shall camp on the side of the dwelling, on the north.
The appointed charge of the sons of Merari is the frames of the dwelling and its bars and its pillars and its sockets and all its equipment — all the work of it —
and the pillars of the court all around, and their sockets and their pegs and their cords.
Moses and Aaron: East

Those camping before the dwelling on the east, before the tent of meeting toward the sunrise, are Moses and Aaron and his sons, keeping the charge of the sanctuary, the charge for the sons of Israel. The outsider who comes near shall be put to death.
All those counted of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the word of the LORD by their clans, every male from a month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand.
The Firstborn Redeemed
The LORD said to Moses, "Count every firstborn male of the sons of Israel from a month old and upward, and take the number of their names.

You shall take the Levites for Me — I am the LORD — in place of every firstborn among the sons of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites in place of every firstborn among the livestock of the sons of Israel."
Moses counted, as the LORD had commanded him, every firstborn among the sons of Israel.
All the firstborn males, by the number of names, from a month old and upward, of those counted, were twenty-two thousand two hundred and seventy-three.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Take the Levites in place of every firstborn among the sons of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites shall be Mine. I am the LORD.
For the redemption of the two hundred and seventy-three of the firstborn of the sons of Israel who are more than the Levites,
you shall take five shekels apiece, head by head. By the shekel of the sanctuary you shall take it; twenty gerahs make a shekel.
You shall give the money to Aaron and to his sons, the redemption of those who are more than their number."
Moses took the redemption money from those who were more than the ones redeemed by the Levites.
From the firstborn of the sons of Israel he took the money, one thousand three hundred and sixty-five shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary.
Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and to his sons at the word of the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

chapters.title: Carrying the Holy Things
chapters.html:
Numbers 4

Kohath

1The LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

2"Take a count of the sons of Kohath from among the sons of Levi, by their clans, by their fathers' house,

3from thirty years old and upward to fifty years old, all who enter the service to do work in the tent of meeting.

4This is the work of the sons of Kohath in the tent of meeting: the most holy things.

5When the camp sets out, Aaron and his sons shall go in and take down the veil of the screen, and cover the ark of the Testimony with it.

6They shall put on it a covering of fine leather, and spread over it a cloth all of blue, and put in its poles.

7Over the table of the Presence they shall spread a cloth of blue, and put on it the dishes and the pans and the bowls and the jars for the drink offering. The continual bread shall be on it.

8They shall spread over them a cloth of crimson, and cover it with a covering of fine leather, and put in its poles.

9They shall take a cloth of blue and cover the lampstand for the light, and its lamps and its tongs and its trays, and all its vessels for oil, with which they serve it.

10They shall put it and all its vessels into a covering of fine leather, and put it on the carrying frame.

11Over the gold altar they shall spread a cloth of blue, and cover it with a covering of fine leather, and put in its poles.

12They shall take all the vessels of service with which they serve in the holy place, and put them in a cloth of blue, and cover them with a covering of fine leather, and put them on the carrying frame.

13They shall clear the ashes from the altar and spread a cloth of purple over it.

14They shall put on it all its vessels with which they serve at it: the fire pans, the forks, the shovels and the basins, all the vessels of the altar. They shall spread over it a covering of fine leather, and put in its poles.

15When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the holy place and all the vessels of the holy place, when the camp sets out, after that the sons of Kohath shall come to carry them. But they shall not touch the holy things, or they will die. These are the load of the sons of Kohath in the tent of meeting.

16The oversight of Eleazar son of Aaron the priest is the oil for the light and the fragrant incense and the regular grain offering and the anointing oil — the oversight of all the dwelling and all that is in it, the holy place and its vessels."

17The LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

18"Do not let the tribe of the clans of the Kohathites be cut off from among the Levites.

19But do this for them, so that they live and do not die when they approach the most holy things: Aaron and his sons shall go in and assign them, each man to his work and to his load.

20But they shall not go in to see the holy things even for an instant, or they will die."

Gershon

21The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

22"Take a count of the sons of Gershon also, by their fathers' house, by their clans.

23From thirty years old and upward to fifty years old you shall count them, all who enter to serve in the service, to do the work in the tent of meeting.

24This is the work of the clans of the Gershonites, in serving and in carrying:

25they shall carry the curtains of the dwelling and the tent of meeting, its covering and the covering of fine leather that is on top of it, and the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting,

26and the hangings of the court, and the screen for the entrance of the gate of the court that is around the dwelling and the altar, and their cords, and all the equipment for their service. Whatever is to be done with them, they shall do.

27At the command of Aaron and his sons shall be all the work of the sons of the Gershonites, in all their load and in all their work. You shall appoint them to the charge of all their load.

28This is the work of the clans of the sons of the Gershonites in the tent of meeting, and their charge is under the hand of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.

Merari

29"The sons of Merari — by their clans, by their fathers' house you shall count them.

30From thirty years old and upward to fifty years old you shall count them, all who enter the service to do the work of the tent of meeting.

31This is the charge of their load, for all their work in the tent of meeting: the frames of the dwelling and its bars and its pillars and its sockets,

32and the pillars of the court all around, and their sockets and their pegs and their cords, with all their equipment and all their work. By name you shall assign the items of the charge of their load.

33This is the work of the clans of the sons of Merari, for all their work in the tent of meeting, under the hand of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest."

The Count

34Moses and Aaron and the chiefs of the congregation counted the sons of the Kohathites by their clans and by their fathers' house,

35from thirty years old and upward to fifty years old, all who enter the service for work in the tent of meeting.

36Those of them counted by their clans were two thousand seven hundred and fifty.

37These are those counted of the clans of the Kohathites, all who work in the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the word of the LORD by the hand of Moses.

38Those counted of the sons of Gershon, by their clans and by their fathers' house,

39from thirty years old and upward to fifty years old, all who enter the service for work in the tent of meeting —

40those of them counted, by their clans, by their fathers' house, were two thousand six hundred and thirty.

41These are those counted of the clans of the sons of Gershon, all who work in the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the word of the LORD.

42Those counted of the clans of the sons of Merari, by their clans, by their fathers' house,

43from thirty years old and upward to fifty years old, all who enter the service for work in the tent of meeting —

44those of them counted by their clans were three thousand two hundred.

45These are those counted of the clans of the sons of Merari, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the word of the LORD by the hand of Moses.

46All those counted of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron and the chiefs of Israel counted, by their clans and by their fathers' house,

47from thirty years old and upward to fifty years old, all who enter to do the work of serving and the work of carrying in the tent of meeting —

48those of them counted were eight thousand five hundred and eighty.

49At the word of the LORD he counted them by the hand of Moses, each man to his work and to his load. They were counted by him, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

Notes

  • v3 "all who enter the service" — kol ba la-tsava, and tsava is the word for an army, the word of the war count in 1:3. Verse 23 doubles it: litsbo tsava, to serve in the service, to muster for duty. The work of carrying the dwelling is counted as a muster, and the women who served in ranks at the entrance of the tent (Exodus 38:8) are described with the same verb.

  • v3 "from thirty years old" — the Greek reads twenty-five here and in vv23, 30, 35, 39, 43 and 47. The Hebrew says thirty in all seven places. In 8:24 the Hebrew itself gives twenty-five as the age a Levite begins. The two ages stand in the Hebrew text as written, and the chapters do not explain the difference.

  • v6 "a covering of fine leather… a cloth all of blue" — on every other item the fine leather goes on the outside. On the ark the order is reversed: the leather goes under, and the blue cloth goes on top, so on the march the ark is the one object seen in blue. The Greek reads tachash, the uncertain word behind fine leather, as a color too: its hyacinth-blue skin.

  • v14 the altar's load — the Greek adds a sentence at the end of this verse: and they shall take a purple cloth and cover the basin and its stand, and put them in a leather covering. The Hebrew has no instructions for the bronze basin anywhere in the chapter.

  • v15 "they shall not touch the holy things, or they will die" — the Kohathites carry the most holy objects and may never see or touch them. The priests wrap everything first, and only then do the carriers come in. When David moves the ark on a cart, Uzzah puts out his hand to steady it and dies (2 Samuel 6:6–7).

  • v18 "do not let the tribe… be cut off" — al takhritu, the verb of the penalty cut off. The command is addressed to Moses and Aaron. If the wrapping is done carelessly, it is the priests who will have cut the Kohathites off.

  • v20 "even for an instant" — ke-valla, literally as a swallowing, the length of a gulp. It occurs nowhere else. The Greek has suddenly.

  • v48 "eight thousand five hundred and eighty" — 2,750 + 2,630 + 3,200. The three clans add up exactly.

chapters.title: The Camp Kept Clean
chapters.html:
Numbers 5

Outside the Camp

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Command the sons of Israel to send out of the camp everyone with blight, and everyone with a discharge, and everyone unclean by a dead person.

3Male and female alike you shall send out; outside the camp you shall send them, so that they do not make their camps unclean, where I dwell among them."

4The sons of Israel did so, and sent them outside the camp. As the LORD had spoken to Moses, so the sons of Israel did.

Wrong Done to a Neighbor

5The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

6"Speak to the sons of Israel: When a man or a woman commits any of the sins people commit, breaking faith with the LORD, and that person is guilty,

7they shall confess the sin they have done. He shall pay back what he is guilty of in full, and add a fifth to it, and give it to the one he wronged.

8But if the man has no redeemer to whom the payment can be made, the payment made to the LORD goes to the priest, besides the ram of atonement with which atonement is made for him.

9Every contribution of all the holy things of the sons of Israel that they bring to the priest shall be his.

10Each man's holy things shall be his own; whatever a man gives to the priest shall be the priest's."

The Water of Bitterness

11The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

12"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: If any man's wife goes astray and breaks faith with him,

13and a man lies with her and it is hidden from her husband's eyes, and she keeps it secret and has made herself unclean, and there is no witness against her, and she was not caught —

14and a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he is jealous of his wife, and she has made herself unclean; or a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he is jealous of his wife, and she has not made herself unclean —

15then the man shall bring his wife to the priest, and bring her offering for her: a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He shall pour no oil on it and put no frankincense on it, because it is a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance, bringing guilt to remembrance.

16The priest shall bring her near and stand her before the LORD.

17The priest shall take holy water in a clay pot, and the priest shall take some of the dust that is on the floor of the dwelling and put it into the water.

18The priest shall stand the woman before the LORD, and let the hair of the woman's head hang loose, and put on her palms the grain offering of remembrance, which is the grain offering of jealousy. In the priest's hand shall be the water of bitterness that brings the curse.

19The priest shall make her swear, and say to the woman, 'If no man has lain with you, and if you have not gone astray into uncleanness while under your husband, be free of this water of bitterness that brings the curse.

20But if you have gone astray while under your husband, and if you have made yourself unclean, and a man other than your husband has lain with you —'

21then the priest shall make the woman swear the oath of the curse, and the priest shall say to the woman, 'the LORD make you a curse and an oath among your people, when the LORD makes your thigh fall away and your belly swell.

22This water that brings the curse shall go into your insides, to make the belly swell and the thigh fall away.' The woman shall say, 'Amen, amen.'

23The priest shall write these curses in a scroll and wash them off into the water of bitterness.

24He shall make the woman drink the water of bitterness that brings the curse, and the water that brings the curse shall go into her and become bitter.

25The priest shall take the grain offering of jealousy from the woman's hand, and wave the grain offering before the LORD, and bring it near to the altar.

26The priest shall take a handful of the grain offering, its memorial portion, and turn it into smoke on the altar, and afterward make the woman drink the water.

27When he has made her drink the water, then, if she has made herself unclean and has broken faith with her husband, the water that brings the curse shall go into her and become bitter, and her belly shall swell and her thigh shall fall away, and the woman shall become a curse among her people.

28But if the woman has not made herself unclean, and she is clean, then she shall be free and shall conceive children.

29This is the instruction for jealousy, when a wife goes astray while under her husband and makes herself unclean,

30or when a spirit of jealousy comes over a man and he is jealous of his wife. He shall stand the woman before the LORD, and the priest shall carry out for her all this instruction.

31The man shall be free of guilt, but that woman shall carry her guilt."

Notes

  • v3 "where I dwell among them" — shokhen, the verb behind mishkan, the dwelling. The camp is clean not because the people are, but because God lives in the middle of it. The three kinds sent out are the three Leviticus laid down: blight (chapters 13–14), discharges (15), and contact with the dead (21:1–4, 22:4).

  • vv6–8 "breaking faith with the LORD" — li-m'ol ma'al, the phrase of Leviticus 6:2, where wronging a neighbor is called breaking faith with God. This law adds what Leviticus left open: if the wronged man has died and has no go'el, no relative to receive the payment (Leviticus 25:25), the debt is not cancelled. It is paid to the LORD, through the priest.

  • v12 "goes astray" — tisteh, from satah, to turn aside from the path. Proverbs uses it of the adulteress: let your heart not turn aside to her ways (7:25). And ma'al, break faith, is the word for betraying God in v6 and for betraying a husband here.

  • v14 "and she has not made herself unclean" — the law is written for both cases, in the same words: the husband's jealousy, and a wife who is guilty, or a wife who is innocent. It does not assume she is guilty. It takes the matter out of the husband's hands and puts it before God.

  • v17 "holy water" — mayim qedoshim occurs here and nowhere else in the Hebrew Bible. The dust is from the floor of the dwelling itself.

  • v22 "Amen, amen" — the first time the word amen appears in the Bible. It is from aman, to be firm, the root of he believed in Genesis 15:6. Saying it, the woman accepts the oath and puts herself in God's hands.

  • v23 "write these curses in a scroll and wash them off" — the curse contains the divine name (v21). The priest writes it and dissolves the ink into the water she drinks. The words themselves go into her.

  • vv21, 27–28 "your thigh fall away and your belly swell" — no one can say exactly what physical condition this names. The outcome for the innocent woman supplies the sense: she shall be free and shall conceive children (v28, literally be sown with seed). The penalty for the guilty is to be unable to bear. No human punishment is prescribed, and none is carried out by the husband or the priest.

speech.text: Numbers 5
Outside the Camp
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Command the sons of Israel to send out of the camp everyone with blight, and everyone with a discharge, and everyone unclean by a dead person.
Male and female alike you shall send out; outside the camp you shall send them, so that they do not make their camps unclean, where I dwell among them."
The sons of Israel did so, and sent them outside the camp. As the LORD had spoken to Moses, so the sons of Israel did.
Wrong Done to a Neighbor
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the sons of Israel: When a man or a woman commits any of the sins people commit, breaking faith with the LORD, and that person is guilty,
they shall confess the sin they have done. He shall pay back what he is guilty of in full, and add a fifth to it, and give it to the one he wronged.
But if the man has no redeemer to whom the payment can be made, the payment made to the LORD goes to the priest, besides the ram of atonement with which atonement is made for him.
Every contribution of all the holy things of the sons of Israel that they bring to the priest shall be his.
Each man's holy things shall be his own; whatever a man gives to the priest shall be the priest's."
The Water of Bitterness
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: If any man's wife goes astray and breaks faith with him,
and a man lies with her and it is hidden from her husband's eyes, and she keeps it secret and has made herself unclean, and there is no witness against her, and she was not caught —

and a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he is jealous of his wife, and she has made herself unclean; or a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he is jealous of his wife, and she has not made herself unclean —

then the man shall bring his wife to the priest, and bring her offering for her: a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He shall pour no oil on it and put no frankincense on it, because it is a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance, bringing guilt to remembrance.
The priest shall bring her near and stand her before the LORD.
The priest shall take holy water in a clay pot, and the priest shall take some of the dust that is on the floor of the dwelling and put it into the water.

The priest shall stand the woman before the LORD, and let the hair of the woman's head hang loose, and put on her palms the grain offering of remembrance, which is the grain offering of jealousy. In the priest's hand shall be the water of bitterness that brings the curse.

The priest shall make her swear, and say to the woman, 'If no man has lain with you, and if you have not gone astray into uncleanness while under your husband, be free of this water of bitterness that brings the curse.
But if you have gone astray while under your husband, and if you have made yourself unclean, and a man other than your husband has lain with you —'

then the priest shall make the woman swear the oath of the curse, and the priest shall say to the woman, 'the LORD make you a curse and an oath among your people, when the LORD makes your thigh fall away and your belly swell.
This water that brings the curse shall go into your insides, to make the belly swell and the thigh fall away.' The woman shall say, 'Amen, amen.'
The priest shall write these curses in a scroll and wash them off into the water of bitterness.
He shall make the woman drink the water of bitterness that brings the curse, and the water that brings the curse shall go into her and become bitter.
The priest shall take the grain offering of jealousy from the woman's hand, and wave the grain offering before the LORD, and bring it near to the altar.
The priest shall take a handful of the grain offering, its memorial portion, and turn it into smoke on the altar, and afterward make the woman drink the water.

When he has made her drink the water, then, if she has made herself unclean and has broken faith with her husband, the water that brings the curse shall go into her and become bitter, and her belly shall swell and her thigh shall fall away, and the woman shall become a curse among her people.
But if the woman has not made herself unclean, and she is clean, then she shall be free and shall conceive children.
This is the instruction for jealousy, when a wife goes astray while under her husband and makes herself unclean,
or when a spirit of jealousy comes over a man and he is jealous of his wife. He shall stand the woman before the LORD, and the priest shall carry out for her all this instruction.
The man shall be free of guilt, but that woman shall carry her guilt."

chapters.title: The Nazirite and the Blessing
chapters.html:
Numbers 6

The Vow of the Nazirite

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When a man or a woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to keep himself apart for the LORD,

3he shall keep apart from wine and strong drink. He shall drink no vinegar made from wine or vinegar made from strong drink, and he shall drink no grape juice of any kind, and he shall eat no grapes, fresh or dried.

4All the days of his separation he shall eat nothing that is made from the grapevine, from the seeds to the skin.

5All the days of his vow of separation no razor shall pass over his head. Until the days are complete for which he keeps himself apart for the LORD, he shall be holy. He shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow long.

6All the days that he keeps himself apart for the LORD, he shall not go near a dead body.

7Not for his father or for his mother, for his brother or for his sister — he shall not make himself unclean for them when they die, because the crown of his God is on his head.

8All the days of his separation he is holy to the LORD.

9If someone dies beside him very suddenly, and he makes his consecrated head unclean, then he shall shave his head on the day of his cleansing. On the seventh day he shall shave it.

10On the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest, to the entrance of the tent of meeting.

11The priest shall offer one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering, and make atonement for him, because he sinned by reason of the dead. He shall make his head holy that same day.

12He shall keep himself apart for the LORD for the days of his separation, and bring a male lamb a year old as a guilt offering. The earlier days shall fall away, because his separation was made unclean.

When the Days Are Complete

13This is the instruction for the Nazirite: On the day the days of his separation are complete, he shall be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting.

14He shall present his offering to the LORD: one unblemished male lamb a year old as a burnt offering, and one unblemished ewe lamb a year old as a sin offering, and one unblemished ram as a peace offering,

15and a basket of unleavened bread, loaves of fine flour mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil, with their grain offering and their drink offerings.

16The priest shall present them before the LORD and offer his sin offering and his burnt offering.

17He shall offer the ram as a sacrifice of peace offering to the LORD, with the basket of unleavened bread. The priest shall offer its grain offering and its drink offering.

18The Nazirite shall shave his consecrated head at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and take the hair of his consecrated head and put it on the fire that is under the sacrifice of the peace offering.

19The priest shall take the boiled shoulder of the ram, and one unleavened loaf from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and put them on the palms of the Nazirite after he has shaved off his consecrated hair.

20The priest shall wave them as a wave offering before the LORD. It is holy for the priest, together with the breast that is waved and the thigh that is lifted off. After that the Nazirite may drink wine.

21This is the instruction for the Nazirite who vows his offering to the LORD for his separation, besides whatever else he can afford. As his vow is that he vows, so he shall do, according to the instruction for his separation."

The Blessing

22The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

23"Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying: This is how you shall bless the sons of Israel. Say to them:

24The LORD bless you and keep you.
25 The LORD make His face shine on you and be gracious to you.
26 The LORD lift up His face toward you and give you peace.

27So they shall put My name on the sons of Israel, and I will bless them."

Notes

  • v2 "the vow of a Nazirite" — nazir, from nazar, to keep apart, the verb of the priests who must keep themselves apart from the holy things when unclean (Leviticus 22:2). The vow is open to a man or a woman, and it is made by choice, for a set time (vv5, 13). The verb for making it is yafli, the special vow of Leviticus 27:2, from the root of pele, wonder.

  • v4 "from the seeds to the skin" — chartsannim and zag occur here and nowhere else. The usual reading is seeds and skins, the two parts of the grape left after pressing. The Greek has them the other way round: from the pressed skins to the seed. Either way the line covers the whole fruit, inside and out.

  • v5 "no razor shall pass over his head" — the words of the angel to Samson's mother: no razor shall go up on his head, for the boy shall be a Nazirite of God from the womb (Judges 13:5). Samson is the one Nazirite made so for life, before birth, by God's word, not his own vow. In the New Testament, John is announced with the other half of this law: wine and strong drink he shall not drink (Luke 1:15), where strong drink is sikera, the Greek form of this verse's shekhar.

  • v7 "the crown of his God is on his head" — nezer, from the same root as nazir, and it is the word for the gold plate on the high priest's turban, the holy crown (Exodus 29:6). The Nazirite keeps the high priest's own rule: he shall not make himself unclean even for his father or for his mother, because the crown of the anointing oil of his God is on him (Leviticus 21:11–12). The high priest's crown is gold; the Nazirite's is his uncut hair.

  • v9 "very suddenly" — be-feta pit'om, suddenly, suddenly: two words for the same thing. The vow can be broken by no act of his own at all, only by being near someone when he dies.

  • v12 "the earlier days shall fall away" — yippelu, they fall. Days kept under the vow before the death do not count, and he begins again from the first day.

  • vv24–26 the blessing — in Hebrew the three lines are three, five and seven words long, each line longer than the one before it. Every line opens with the name of the LORD. The you is singular throughout: the priests bless the whole people as if it were one person.

  • vv25–26 "make His face shine… lift up His face" — panav, His face, twice. In Leviticus 26:17 God warned, I will set My face against you. The blessing asks for the reverse. Lift up the face toward someone is to look on them with favor. Peace is shalom, which is more than the absence of war: whole, complete, lacking nothing.

  • v27 "they shall put My name on the sons of Israel" — the priests speak the words, and God says what they do: the name YHWH, spoken three times, is put on the people. And the last word is His: and I will bless them. The priests speak, and God is the one who blesses.

chapters.title: The Gifts of the Twelve Chiefs
chapters.html:
Numbers 7

Wagons for the Levites

1And it came to pass, on the day Moses finished setting up the dwelling and had anointed it and set it apart with all its vessels, and the altar with all its vessels,

2that the chiefs of Israel, the heads of their fathers' houses, presented offerings. They were the chiefs of the tribes, the men who stood over those who were counted.

3They brought their offering before the LORD: six covered wagons and twelve oxen, a wagon for every two chiefs and an ox for each one. They presented them before the dwelling.

4The LORD said to Moses,

5"Accept these from them, and let them be used for the work of the tent of meeting. Give them to the Levites, to each according to his work."

6So Moses took the wagons and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.

7He gave two wagons and four oxen to the sons of Gershon, as their work required,

8and four wagons and eight oxen to the sons of Merari, as their work required, under the hand of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.

9But to the sons of Kohath he gave none, because theirs was the service of the holy things, which they carried on their shoulders.

One Chief Each Day

10The chiefs brought their offerings for the dedication of the altar on the day it was anointed, and presented them before the altar.

11The LORD said to Moses, "Let them present their offerings for the dedication of the altar one chief each day."

The First Day: Judah

12The one who presented his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah.

13His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;

14one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;

15one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;

16one male goat for a sin offering;

17and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.

The Second Day: Issachar

18On the second day Nethanel son of Zuar, the chief of Issachar, presented an offering.

19He presented as his offering one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;

20one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;

21one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;

22one male goat for a sin offering;

23and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Nethanel son of Zuar.

The Third Day: Zebulun

24On the third day it was the chief of the sons of Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon.

25His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;

26one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;

27one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;

28one male goat for a sin offering;

29and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Eliab son of Helon.

The Fourth Day: Reuben

30On the fourth day it was the chief of the sons of Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur.

31His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;

32one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;

33one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;

34one male goat for a sin offering;

35and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Elizur son of Shedeur.

The Fifth Day: Simeon

37His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;

38one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;

39one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;

40one male goat for a sin offering;

41and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.

The Sixth Day: Gad

44one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;

The Seventh Day: Ephraim

The Ninth Day: Benjamin

60On the ninth day it was the chief of the sons of Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni.

61His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;

The Tenth Day: Dan

66On the tenth day it was the chief of the sons of Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.

68one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;

71and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.

The Eleventh Day: Asher

72On the eleventh day it was the chief of the sons of Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran.

73His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;

74one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;

75one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;

76one male goat for a sin offering;

77and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Pagiel son of Ocran.

The Twelfth Day: Naphtali

78On the twelfth day it was the chief of the sons of Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.

79His offering was one silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;

80one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense;

81one young bull, one ram, one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;

82one male goat for a sin offering;

83and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Ahira son of Enan.

The Whole Gift

84This was the dedication offering for the altar from the chiefs of Israel, on the day it was anointed: twelve silver dishes, twelve silver basins, twelve gold pans,

85each silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and each basin seventy. All the silver of the vessels was two thousand four hundred shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary.

86The twelve gold pans full of incense weighed ten shekels each, by the shekel of the sanctuary. All the gold of the pans was a hundred and twenty shekels.

87All the cattle for the burnt offering: twelve bulls, twelve rams, twelve male lambs a year old, with their grain offering; and twelve male goats for a sin offering.

88All the cattle for the sacrifice of peace offerings: twenty-four bulls, sixty rams, sixty he-goats, sixty male lambs a year old. This was the dedication offering for the altar after it was anointed.

The Voice from Above the Cover

89When Moses went into the tent of meeting to speak with Him, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the cover that was on the ark of the Testimony, from between the two cherubim; and He spoke to him.

Notes

  • v1 "on the day Moses finished setting up the dwelling" — the chapter goes back in time. The dwelling was set up on the first day of the first month of the second year (Exodus 40:17); Numbers began a month later, in the second month (1:1). These gifts arrived in the days after the dwelling was raised, and the book tells of them here, after the camp has been counted and ordered.

  • vv3, 9 "covered wagons… on their shoulders" — agalah, a wagon. The Kohathites got none, because the most holy things are carried by hand (4:15). When David first moved the ark, it was put on a new cart, the same word (2 Samuel 6:3), and Uzzah died. The second time, the Levites carried the ark of God on their shoulders with the poles, as Moses had commanded (1 Chronicles 15:15), and David said of the first attempt, we did not seek Him in the way He ruled (15:13).

  • v10 "the dedication of the altar" — chanukkat ha-mizbeach. Chanukkah is the word that later named the festival of the rededicated temple. The Greek here has enkainismos, and the Gospel of John calls that festival by a word from the same root, ta enkainia: it was the feast of Dedication at Jerusalem; it was winter (John 10:22).

  • vv12–83 the same gift twelve times — each chief brings exactly what the others bring, and the text writes it out in full every time, six verses a day for twelve days, rather than saying and so did the rest. No tribe's gift is summarized into another's. Only the first is introduced differently: Nahshon of Judah is not called chief (v12), and every other man is.

  • vv17, 88 "he-goats… male goat" — two Hebrew words. The sin offering is a se'ir izzim, a male goat (v16); the peace offering includes attudim, he-goats, the word Jacob used of the flock's breeding males (Genesis 31:10).

  • vv84–88 the totals — twelve dishes of 130 shekels and twelve basins of 70 come to 2,400 shekels of silver; twelve pans of 10 come to 120 of gold; and 2 oxen, 5 rams, 5 he-goats and 5 lambs a day for twelve days make 24, 60, 60 and 60. Every total in these verses adds up.

  • v89 "from above the cover… from between the two cherubim" — the promise of Exodus 25:22, I will meet with you there, and I will speak with you from above the cover, from between the two cherubim, kept here for the first time in the words it was made in. The chapter of gifts ends with the voice.

chapters.title: The Lamps and the Levites
chapters.html:
Numbers 8

The Seven Lamps

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Speak to Aaron and say to him: When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps shall give their light toward the front of the lampstand."

3Aaron did so. He set up its lamps to face the front of the lampstand, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

4This is how the lampstand was made: hammered work of gold, hammered work from its base to its flowers. Just as the LORD had shown Moses, so he made the lampstand.

The Levites Made Clean

5The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

6"Take the Levites from among the sons of Israel and cleanse them.

7This is what you shall do to them to cleanse them: sprinkle the water of purification on them, and have them shave their whole body and wash their clothes, and so cleanse themselves.

8Then they shall take a young bull and its grain offering, fine flour mixed with oil, and you shall take a second young bull for a sin offering.

9You shall bring the Levites before the tent of meeting and assemble the whole congregation of the sons of Israel.

10When you bring the Levites before the LORD, the sons of Israel shall lean their hands on the Levites.

11Aaron shall present the Levites before the LORD as a wave offering from the sons of Israel, so that they may do the service of the LORD.

12The Levites shall lean their hands on the heads of the bulls, and you shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the LORD, to make atonement for the Levites.

13You shall stand the Levites before Aaron and before his sons, and present them as a wave offering to the LORD.

14So you shall set the Levites apart from among the sons of Israel, and the Levites shall be Mine.

15After that the Levites shall go in to serve at the tent of meeting, once you have cleansed them and presented them as a wave offering.

Given in Place of the Firstborn

16For they are wholly given to Me from among the sons of Israel. In place of all who open the womb, the firstborn of all the sons of Israel, I have taken them for Myself.

17For every firstborn among the sons of Israel is Mine, of man and of beast. On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I set them apart for Myself,

18and I have taken the Levites in place of every firstborn among the sons of Israel.

19I have given the Levites, wholly given, to Aaron and to his sons from among the sons of Israel, to do the service of the sons of Israel at the tent of meeting and to make atonement for the sons of Israel, so that there will be no plague among the sons of Israel when the sons of Israel come near the holy place."

20Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation of the sons of Israel did so to the Levites. As the LORD had commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so the sons of Israel did to them.

21The Levites purified themselves and washed their clothes, and Aaron presented them as a wave offering before the LORD and made atonement for them to cleanse them.

22After that the Levites went in to do their service at the tent of meeting before Aaron and before his sons. As the LORD had commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so they did to them.

Twenty-Five to Fifty

23The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

24"This is what applies to the Levites: from twenty-five years old and upward a man shall come to serve in the service of the tent of meeting.

25From the age of fifty he shall leave the service of the work and serve no more.

26He may assist his brothers at the tent of meeting in keeping the charge, but he shall do no work. This is how you shall deal with the Levites in their duties."

Notes

  • v2 "when you set up the lamps" — be-ha'alotekha, literally when you make them go up: the verb alah, which also names the burnt offering, the olah, the offering that goes up (Leviticus 1:3). The flame is spoken of as something raised.

  • v4 "just as the LORD had shown Moses" — Exodus 25:40 closes the instructions for the lampstand with see, and make them by their pattern, which you are being shown on the mountain. Here the finished lampstand is said to match what Moses was shown.

  • v7 "the water of purification" — mei chattat, literally water of sin: the noun that names the sin and also the sin offering. It is the water that takes sin away, as the verb chitte means to purge sin out of something (Leviticus 6:26, 8:15).

  • v10 "the sons of Israel shall lean their hands on the Levites" — ve-samkhu, the verb of the worshipper leaning his hand on the head of his animal (Leviticus 1:4). Here the people lean their hands on men, and in the next verse those men are presented as a wave offering. The Levites are given to God the way an offering is given, standing in for the firstborn of every family (vv16–18).

  • v11 "as a wave offering" — tenufah, the word for the breast of the peace offering waved before the LORD and given to the priests (Leviticus 7:30, 34). It is used of the Levites four times in this chapter (vv11, 13, 15, 21), and they are given to Aaron (3:9, and v19 here): an offering that goes to the priests, as the breast does.

  • v19 "the sons of Israel," five times — the phrase is repeated five times in one verse, where one mention and pronouns would have done. The verse is about who is served and protected, and it names them every time.

  • v24 "from twenty-five years old" — 4:3 gave the age as thirty, in the Hebrew of all seven verses there. Here the Hebrew itself says twenty-five. The Greek has twenty-five in both places.

  • vv25–26 "he shall leave the service… he may assist his brothers" — yashuv, he shall turn back from the service, and then sheret et echav, he shall serve alongside his brothers. The man over fifty is not dismissed. He stops the carrying (4:15, 24) and stays at the tent to keep the charge.

chapters.title: The Second Passover and the Cloud
chapters.html:
Numbers 9

The Passover at Sinai

1The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt, saying,

2"Let the sons of Israel keep the Passover at its appointed time.

3On the fourteenth day of this month, between the evenings, you shall keep it at its appointed time. You shall keep it according to all its statutes and all its rulings."

4So Moses told the sons of Israel to keep the Passover.

5They kept the Passover in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, between the evenings, in the wilderness of Sinai. Just as the LORD had commanded Moses, so the sons of Israel did.

Men Who Could Not Keep It

6But there were men who were unclean because of a human corpse, and they could not keep the Passover on that day. So they came before Moses and Aaron that same day,

7and those men said to him, "We are unclean because of a human corpse. Why should we be kept back from presenting the LORD's offering at its appointed time among the sons of Israel?"

8Moses said to them, "Wait, and I will hear what the LORD commands concerning you."

9The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

10"Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: If any one of you or of your generations is unclean because of a corpse, or is away on a long journey, he shall still keep the Passover to the LORD.

11In the second month, on the fourteenth day, between the evenings, they shall keep it. They shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

12They shall leave none of it until morning, and they shall not break a bone of it. They shall keep it according to every statute of the Passover.

13But the man who is clean and is not on a journey, and fails to keep the Passover — that person shall be cut off from his people, because he did not present the LORD's offering at its appointed time. That man shall carry his sin.

14If a guest lives among you and would keep the Passover to the LORD, he shall keep it according to the statute of the Passover and its ruling. You shall have one statute, for the guest and for the native of the land."

The Cloud over the Dwelling

15On the day the dwelling was set up, the cloud covered the dwelling, the tent of the Testimony; and from evening until morning it was over it like the appearance of fire.

16So it was continually: the cloud covered it, and at night the appearance of fire.

17Whenever the cloud lifted from over the tent, the sons of Israel would set out after it; and in the place where the cloud settled, there the sons of Israel would camp.

18At the command of the LORD the sons of Israel set out, and at the command of the LORD they camped. As long as the cloud rested on the dwelling, they stayed in camp.

19When the cloud lingered over the dwelling many days, the sons of Israel kept the LORD's charge and did not set out.

20Sometimes the cloud was over the dwelling only a few days; at the command of the LORD they camped, and at the command of the LORD they set out.

21Sometimes the cloud stayed from evening until morning; and when the cloud lifted in the morning, they set out. Or it stayed a day and a night, and when the cloud lifted, they set out.

22Whether it was two days, or a month, or longer, while the cloud lingered over the dwelling and rested on it, the sons of Israel stayed in camp and did not set out; but when it lifted, they set out.

23At the command of the LORD they camped, and at the command of the LORD they set out. They kept the LORD's charge at the command of the LORD, through Moses.

Notes

  • v1 "in the first month of the second year" — a month before the count that opens the book (1:1, the second month). Like 7:1, this chapter reaches back in time. It is the first Passover kept since the night in Egypt, and the only one the five books record in the wilderness.

  • vv6–7 "Why should we be kept back?" — lamah nigara, why should we be made less, cut short. The men are not asking to be excused from the Passover; they are asking not to miss it. Nothing in the law so far covered them, and Moses does not answer from what he knows. He says wait, and I will hear (v8).

  • v10 "a long journey" — in the Hebrew text the last letter of rechoqah, long (literally far), has a dot written over it. It is one of ten places in the five books where the scribes marked a word or letter this way (3:39 is another). The dot flags the letter as questioned. The text does not say why.

  • vv10–11 the second Passover — a month later, on the fourteenth of the second month, for anyone who was unclean or far away on the first date. It is the only festival in the Torah that is given a second date.

  • v12 "they shall not break a bone of it" — the rule of the first Passover (Exodus 12:46), repeated for the second. John quotes it at the cross, when the soldiers do not break Jesus' legs: these things happened so that the Scripture would be fulfilled: not a bone of him shall be broken (John 19:36).

  • v14 "one statute, for the guest and for the native" — the guest who keeps the Passover keeps it by the same law. Exodus 12:48 had set the condition, that his males be circumcised first.

  • vv18–23 "at the command of the LORD" — al pi YHWH, literally at the mouth of the LORD, seven times in six verses (twice in v18, twice in v20, three times in v23). Whether the cloud stayed one night or a year (v22, yamim, "days", which can mean a year, as in Leviticus 25:29), the camp moved when it moved and not before.

  • v18 "as long as the cloud rested on the dwelling" — the verb is shakhan, to settle, to dwell, the root of mishkan, the dwelling itself. The cloud dwells on the dwelling.
