chapters.title: The Trumpets, and Leaving Sinai
chapters.html:
Numbers 10

Two Silver Trumpets

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Make yourself two trumpets of silver; you shall make them of hammered work. They shall be for you to summon the congregation and to set the camps moving.

3When both are blown, the whole congregation shall gather to you at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

4If only one is blown, the chiefs, the heads of the thousands of Israel, shall gather to you.

5When you sound a blast, the camps on the east side shall set out.

6When you sound a second blast, the camps on the south side shall set out. A blast shall be sounded for their setting out.

7But when the assembly is to be gathered, you shall blow, but not sound a blast.

8The sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow the trumpets. They shall be a lasting statute for you through your generations.

9When you go to war in your land against the enemy who oppresses you, you shall sound a blast on the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the LORD your God and saved from your enemies.

10On your days of gladness, at your appointed times and at the beginnings of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over your sacrifices of peace offerings, and they shall be a remembrance for you before your God. I am the LORD your God."

Setting Out

11And it came to pass in the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth of the month, that the cloud lifted from over the dwelling of the Testimony.

12The sons of Israel set out on their journeys from the wilderness of Sinai, and the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.

13They set out for the first time at the command of the LORD through Moses.

14The banner of the camp of the sons of Judah set out first, by their divisions; over its army was Nahshon son of Amminadab.

15Over the army of the tribe of the sons of Issachar was Nethanel son of Zuar,

16and over the army of the tribe of the sons of Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon.

17Then the dwelling was taken down, and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, who carried the dwelling, set out.

18Then the banner of the camp of Reuben set out, by their divisions; over its army was Elizur son of Shedeur.

19Over the army of the tribe of the sons of Simeon was Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai,

20and over the army of the tribe of the sons of Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel.

21Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things; and the dwelling was set up before they arrived.

22Then the banner of the camp of the sons of Ephraim set out, by their divisions; over its army was Elishama son of Ammihud.

23Over the army of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh was Gamaliel son of Pedahzur,

24and over the army of the tribe of the sons of Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni.

25Then the banner of the camp of the sons of Dan set out, the rear guard of all the camps, by their divisions; over its army was Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.

26Over the army of the tribe of the sons of Asher was Pagiel son of Ocran,

27and over the army of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.

28This was the order of march of the sons of Israel by their divisions when they set out.

Hobab

29Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses' father-in-law, "We are setting out for the place of which the LORD said, 'I will give it to you.' Come with us, and we will do you good, for the LORD has promised good to Israel."

30But he said to him, "I will not go. I will go back to my own land and my own kindred."

31He said, "Please do not leave us, because you know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you will be eyes for us.

32If you go with us, then whatever good the LORD does for us, we will do the same for you."

The Ark Goes Ahead

33So they set out from the mountain of the LORD a three days' journey, and the ark of the covenant of the LORD went before them those three days, to seek out a resting place for them.

34The cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp.

35Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say,
"Rise up, O LORD, and let Your enemies be scattered,
and let those who hate You flee before You."

36When it came to rest, he would say,
"Return, O LORD,
to the countless thousands of Israel."

Notes

  • vv5–7 "sound a blast… blow, but not sound a blast" — two verbs. Taqa is to blow the trumpet; heri'a is to sound the teru'ah, the blast or great shout of Leviticus 23:24 and 25:9. The assembly is called by the one, and the camp is set moving by the other.

  • v9 "you will be remembered before the LORD" — ve-nizkartem, the verb zakhar. The trumpets are blown in war and at the feasts alike, and both times the stated purpose is that God remember (v10, a remembrance before your God).

  • v11 "in the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth" — Israel reached Sinai in the third month after leaving Egypt (Exodus 19:1). They leave it now, nineteen days after the count of 1:1: almost a year at the mountain. Exodus 19 through Numbers 10 all happens in that one year.

  • v21 "carrying the holy things" — the Hebrew says nos'ei ha-miqdash, carrying the sanctuary: the Kohathites carried the ark and the most holy things (4:4–15). The Gershonites and Merarites went ahead with the structure (v17), so that the dwelling was already standing when the holy things arrived.

  • v29 "Hobab son of Reuel… Moses' father-in-law" — the Hebrew allows either man to be the father-in-law. Exodus calls the priest of Midian Reuel (2:18) and Jethro (3:1). Judges 4:11 calls Hobab the father-in-law of Moses. The verse can be read either way, and the text does not settle which man is meant.

  • v31 "you will be eyes for us" — he knows the wilderness and can show them where to camp. The Greek reads differently: and you will be an elder among us.

  • v33 "to seek out a resting place" — la-tur, to scout, the verb used for the twelve men sent to spy out Canaan (13:2). The ark goes ahead of the people as a scout.

  • vv35–36 "Rise up, O LORD, and let Your enemies be scattered" — Psalm 68 opens with the same words, turned to the third person: let God rise up, let His enemies be scattered, and let those who hate Him flee before Him (68:1). Countless thousands is rivevot alfei, the ten thousands of thousands; on thousands, see the note on 1:16.

speech.text: Numbers 10
Two Silver Trumpets
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Make yourself two trumpets of silver; you shall make them of hammered work. They shall be for you to summon the congregation and to set the camps moving.
When both are blown, the whole congregation shall gather to you at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
If only one is blown, the chiefs, the heads of the thousands of Israel, shall gather to you.
When you sound a blast, the camps on the east side shall set out.
When you sound a second blast, the camps on the south side shall set out. A blast shall be sounded for their setting out.
But when the assembly is to be gathered, you shall blow, but not sound a blast.
The sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow the trumpets. They shall be a lasting statute for you through your generations.
When you go to war in your land against the enemy who oppresses you, you shall sound a blast on the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the LORD your God and saved from your enemies.

On your days of gladness, at your appointed times and at the beginnings of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over your sacrifices of peace offerings, and they shall be a remembrance for you before your God. I am the LORD your God."
Setting Out
And it came to pass in the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth of the month, that the cloud lifted from over the dwelling of the Testimony.
The sons of Israel set out on their journeys from the wilderness of Sinai, and the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.
They set out for the first time at the command of the LORD through Moses.
The banner of the camp of the sons of Judah set out first, by their divisions; over its army was Nahshon son of Amminadab.
Over the army of the tribe of the sons of Issachar was Nethanel son of Zuar,
and over the army of the tribe of the sons of Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon.
Then the dwelling was taken down, and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, who carried the dwelling, set out.
Then the banner of the camp of Reuben set out, by their divisions; over its army was Elizur son of Shedeur.
Over the army of the tribe of the sons of Simeon was Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai,
and over the army of the tribe of the sons of Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel.
Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things; and the dwelling was set up before they arrived.
Then the banner of the camp of the sons of Ephraim set out, by their divisions; over its army was Elishama son of Ammihud.
Over the army of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh was Gamaliel son of Pedahzur,
and over the army of the tribe of the sons of Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni.
Then the banner of the camp of the sons of Dan set out, the rear guard of all the camps, by their divisions; over its army was Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
Over the army of the tribe of the sons of Asher was Pagiel son of Ocran,
and over the army of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.
This was the order of march of the sons of Israel by their divisions when they set out.
Hobab

Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses' father-in-law, "We are setting out for the place of which the LORD said, 'I will give it to you.' Come with us, and we will do you good, for the LORD has promised good to Israel."
But he said to him, "I will not go. I will go back to my own land and my own kindred."
He said, "Please do not leave us, because you know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you will be eyes for us.
If you go with us, then whatever good the LORD does for us, we will do the same for you."
The Ark Goes Ahead
So they set out from the mountain of the LORD a three days' journey, and the ark of the covenant of the LORD went before them those three days, to seek out a resting place for them.
The cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp.
Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say, "Rise up, O LORD, and let Your enemies be scattered, and let those who hate You flee before You."
When it came to rest, he would say, "Return, O LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel."

chapters.title: The Graves of Craving
chapters.html:
Numbers 11

Taberah

1The people became complainers, and it was evil in the hearing of the LORD. The LORD heard, and His anger burned, and the fire of the LORD burned among them and consumed some at the edge of the camp.

2The people cried out to Moses, and Moses prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down.

3The name of that place was called Taberah, because the fire of the LORD had burned among them.

Who Will Give Us Meat?

4The rabble among them felt a craving, and the sons of Israel also wept again and said, "Who will give us meat to eat?

5We remember the fish we ate in Egypt for nothing, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions and the garlic.

6But now our throat is dried up. There is nothing at all — nothing but this manna to look at."

7Now the manna was like coriander seed, and it looked like bdellium.

8The people went about and gathered it, and ground it with millstones or pounded it in a mortar, and boiled it in pots and made cakes of it. It tasted like cakes made with rich oil.

9When the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna fell with it.

Moses Cannot Carry Them

10Moses heard the people weeping, family by family, each man at the entrance of his tent. The anger of the LORD burned hot, and in Moses' eyes it was evil.

11Moses said to the LORD, "Why have You brought trouble on Your servant? Why have I not found favor in Your eyes, that You lay the burden of all this people on me?

12Did I conceive all this people? Did I give birth to them, that You should say to me, 'Carry them in your arms, as a nurse carries a nursing child,' to the land You swore to their fathers?

13Where am I to get meat to give all this people? For they weep before me, saying, 'Give us meat, and let us eat.'

14I cannot carry all this people by myself. It is too heavy for me.

15If this is how You will treat me, kill me now, if I have found favor in Your eyes, and let me not see my misery."

Seventy Elders

16The LORD said to Moses, "Gather for Me seventy men of the elders of Israel, whom you know to be elders of the people and its officers, and take them to the tent of meeting, and let them stand there with you.

17I will come down and speak with you there, and I will take some of the spirit that is on you and put it on them. They shall carry the burden of the people with you, so that you do not carry it by yourself.

18Say to the people: Set yourselves apart for tomorrow, and you shall eat meat. For you have wept in the hearing of the LORD, saying, 'Who will give us meat to eat? For it was good for us in Egypt.' So the LORD will give you meat, and you shall eat.

19You shall eat it not one day, or two days, or five days, or ten days, or twenty days,

20but a whole month, until it comes out of your nostrils and becomes disgusting to you — because you have rejected the LORD who is among you, and have wept before Him, saying, 'Why did we ever come out of Egypt?'"

21Moses said, "The people I am among number six hundred thousand on foot, and You have said, 'I will give them meat, and they shall eat for a whole month.'

22If flocks and herds were slaughtered for them, would it be enough for them? If all the fish of the sea were gathered for them, would it be enough for them?"

23The LORD said to Moses, "Is the LORD's hand too short? Now you will see whether My word comes true for you or not."

24So Moses went out and told the people the words of the LORD. He gathered seventy men of the elders of the people and stood them around the tent.

25The LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and took some of the spirit that was on him and put it on the seventy elders. When the spirit rested on them, they prophesied; but they did not do so again.

Eldad and Medad

26But two men had stayed in the camp, one named Eldad and the other named Medad, and the spirit rested on them. They were among those written down, but they had not gone out to the tent, and they prophesied in the camp.

27A young man ran and told Moses, "Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!"

28Joshua son of Nun, Moses' assistant from his youth, answered and said, "My lord Moses, stop them!"

29But Moses said to him, "Are you jealous for my sake? If only all the LORD's people were prophets, and the LORD would put His spirit on them!"

30Moses went back to the camp, he and the elders of Israel.

The Quail

31A wind went out from the LORD and swept quail in from the sea and let them fall beside the camp, about a day's journey on this side and a day's journey on that side, all around the camp, about two cubits above the ground.

32The people rose up all that day and all night and all the next day and gathered the quail. The one who gathered least gathered ten homers. They spread them out all around the camp.

33The meat was still between their teeth, before it was chewed, when the anger of the LORD burned against the people, and the LORD struck the people with a very great plague.

34The name of that place was called Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had the craving.

35From Kibroth-hattaavah the people set out for Hazeroth, and they stayed at Hazeroth.

Notes

  • v1 "became complainers" — ke-mit'onenim, a form that occurs here and nowhere else in the Bible, and it comes with the little word ke, like: the people were like complainers, or acted as complainers. The text does not say what they complained about. It says only that it was evil in the hearing of the LORD.

  • v4 "the rabble" — ha-asafsuf, another word found only here. It is built from asaf, to gather, doubled: the gathered-up crowd, the ones who were swept along. Exodus 12:38 used a different phrase, erev rav, for the great mixed crowd that came out with Israel. The rabble start the craving, and the sons of Israel also take it up.

  • vv4, 34 "felt a craving… the people who had the craving" — hit'avu ta'avah, they craved a craving, and the place is named for it: Kibroth-hattaavah, the Graves of Craving. The word that began the chapter's trouble becomes the name on its graves.

  • v6 "our throat is dried up" — nafshenu yeveshah. Nefesh is the throat and the appetite before it is the soul, and here the plain sense is right on the surface: the throat is dry, and nothing to swallow but manna.

  • v7 "like bdellium" — bedolach, named with gold and onyx in the land of Havilah, by the river of Eden (Genesis 2:12). Exodus 16:31 said the manna was white and tasted like wafers with honey. Here it tastes like cakes made with oil.

  • v12 "as a nurse carries a nursing child" — Moses pictures himself as the mother, did I conceive… did I give birth, and then as the one who carries the baby. Omen, nurse, is a masculine noun, a man who carries and raises a child: kings shall be your nurses (Isaiah 49:23).

  • v15 "if this is how You will treat me" — the Hebrew pronoun is at, you, in its feminine form, with a masculine verb beside it. The text does not explain it.

  • vv17, 25–29, 31 "spirit… wind" — ruach, one word for both. God takes some of the ruach on Moses and puts it on the seventy (v25); it rests on Eldad and Medad (v26); Moses wishes God would put His ruach on all the people (v29). Then a ruach goes out from the LORD and brings the quail (v31). The same word carries the gift and the judgment.

  • v23 "Is the LORD's hand too short?" — the question Isaiah answers twice: the LORD's hand is not too short to save (59:1, and 50:2).

  • v28 "Moses' assistant from his youth" — mi-bechurav, which can mean from his youth or one of his chosen men. The Greek takes the second: the chosen one.

  • v31 "about two cubits above the ground" — about three feet. The Hebrew does not say whether the quail flew that low, or lay that deep. The Greek has the same words, about two cubits from the ground.

chapters.title: Miriam, Aaron, and Moses
chapters.html:
Numbers 12

Against Moses

1Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Cushite woman he had married — for he had married a Cushite woman.

2They said, "Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Has He not spoken through us too?" The LORD heard it.

3Now the man Moses was very humble, more than any person on the face of the earth.

4Suddenly the LORD said to Moses and to Aaron and to Miriam, "Come out, the three of you, to the tent of meeting." The three of them came out.

5The LORD came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the tent, and called Aaron and Miriam, and the two of them came forward.

6He said, "Hear My words:
If there is a prophet among you,
I the LORD make Myself known to him in a vision;
I speak with him in a dream.

7Not so with My servant Moses.
He is trusted in all My house.

8Mouth to mouth I speak with him,
plainly and not in riddles,
and he sees the form of the LORD.
Why then were you not afraid
to speak against My servant Moses?"

9The anger of the LORD burned against them, and He went away.

White as Snow

10The cloud turned away from over the tent, and here — Miriam was blighted, white as snow. Aaron turned toward Miriam, and here — she was blighted.

11Aaron said to Moses, "Please, my lord, do not hold against us the sin we committed in our folly.

12Do not let her be like a dead thing, whose flesh is half eaten away when it comes out of its mother's womb."

13Moses cried out to the LORD, saying, "O God, please heal her, please."

14The LORD said to Moses, "If her father had spit in her face, would she not be put to shame seven days? Let her be shut away outside the camp seven days, and afterward she may be brought back in."

15So Miriam was shut away outside the camp seven days, and the people did not set out until Miriam was brought back in.

16Afterward the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.

Notes

  • v1 "the Cushite woman" — ha-ishah ha-kushit. Cush is the land south of Egypt, the country of the Gihon in Genesis 2:13 and a son of Ham in Genesis 10:6. The Greek reads the Ethiopian woman, Aithiopissa, twice in this verse. Whether she is Zipporah, the Midianite wife of Exodus 2:21, or a second wife, the text does not say. Habakkuk puts the two names side by side, the tents of Cushan… the curtains of the land of Midian (3:7).

  • v1 "Miriam and Aaron spoke" — the verb is feminine singular, va-tedabber, she spoke, with Aaron added after it. Miriam leads, and in v10 she alone is struck.

  • v3 "very humble" — anav. The written text spells it without the letter yod, and the reading tradition adds it: one of the places where the written and the read forms differ. The word is from the root of ani, the poor and lowly: a man who does not defend himself, and here the LORD defends him.

  • v7 "He is trusted in all My house" — ne'eman, faithful, trusted, from aman, the root of amen. The letter to the Hebrews quotes it: Moses was faithful in all His house as a servant (Hebrews 3:5).

  • v8 "Mouth to mouth… he sees the form of the LORD" — temunat YHWH. At Horeb the people heard the sound of words, but saw no form, the same word (Deuteronomy 4:12). Moses sees what the people did not. The Greek has he saw the glory of the Lord.

  • v10 "white as snow" — metsora'at ka-shaleg, the words of Exodus 4:6, where the LORD made Moses' own hand blighted, white as snow as a sign, and then healed it.

  • v13 "O God, please heal her, please" — El na refa na lah, five words in Hebrew, and the only thing Moses says in the chapter. The man who was spoken against prays for the one who spoke.

  • v14 "If her father had spit in her face" — ve-aviha yaroq yaraq be-faneha. A father's public contempt would shame a daughter seven days, and so her shutting away is seven days: the seven days of Leviticus 13:4–5. The camp waits for her (v15).

chapters.title: The Twelve Scouts
chapters.html:
Numbers 13

One Man from Each Tribe

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Send men to scout out the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the sons of Israel. You shall send one man from each tribe of their fathers, every one a chief among them."

3So Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran at the command of the LORD, all of them men who were heads of the sons of Israel.

4These were their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;

5from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori;

6from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;

7from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;

8from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;

9from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;

10from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;

11from the tribe of Joseph, that is, from the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi;

12from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;

13from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;

14from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;

15from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.

16These are the names of the men Moses sent to scout out the land. Moses called Hoshea son of Nun Joshua.

What to Look For

17So Moses sent them to scout out the land of Canaan, and said to them, "Go up this way into the Negev, and go up into the hill country,

18and see what the land is like, and whether the people who live in it are strong or weak, few or many,

19and whether the land they live in is good or bad, and whether the cities they live in are open camps or fortified,

20and whether the land is rich or poor, and whether there are trees in it or not. Be brave, and bring back some of the fruit of the land." Now it was the season of the first ripe grapes.

Forty Days

21So they went up and scouted out the land from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, near Lebo-hamath.

22They went up into the Negev, and he came to Hebron. Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai, the descendants of Anak, were there. Now Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.

23They came to the valley of Eshcol, and cut down from there a branch with a single cluster of grapes, and they carried it on a pole between two of them, with some of the pomegranates and the figs.

24That place was called the valley of Eshcol because of the cluster that the sons of Israel cut down there.

25They came back from scouting out the land at the end of forty days.

The Report

26They came to Moses and Aaron and to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel in the wilderness of Paran, at Kadesh. They brought back word to them and to the whole congregation, and showed them the fruit of the land.

27They told him, "We came to the land where you sent us, and it does flow with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.

28But the people who live in the land are strong, and the cities are fortified and very large. We saw the descendants of Anak there too.

29The Amalekites live in the land of the Negev; the Hittites, the Jebusites and the Amorites live in the hill country; and the Canaanites live by the sea and along the Jordan."

30Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said, "We must go up at once and take possession of it, because we can surely overcome it."

31But the men who had gone up with him said, "We cannot go up against the people, because they are stronger than we are."

32They spread among the sons of Israel a bad report of the land they had scouted, saying, "The land we passed through to scout it out is a land that devours those who live in it, and all the people we saw in it are men of great size.

33There we saw the Nephilim — the sons of Anak are from the Nephilim — and we were like grasshoppers in our own eyes, and so we were in theirs."

Notes

  • v2 "to scout out" — ve-yaturu, from tur, to go about and look over. The ark did this for the people in 10:33, to seek out a resting place. And in 15:39 the same verb warns against the scouts' failure: you shall not go about after your own heart and your own eyes.

  • v16 "Moses called Hoshea son of Nun Joshua" — Hoshea is he saves; Yehoshua adds the name of God: the LORD saves. Moses adds one letter, and the man who will lead Israel into the land carries the LORD's name in his own. The Greek of Yehoshua is Iēsous, Jesus (see the note on Exodus 17:9).

  • v22 "and he came to Hebron" — the verb is singular in the middle of a plural story: they went up… and he came. The text does not say who. Caleb, who later asks for Hebron as his own (Joshua 14:12–14), is the one it is usually taken to mean.

  • v22 "seven years before Zoan in Egypt" — a builder's date: Hebron was older than a city of Egypt by seven years.

  • vv23–24 "the valley of Eshcol… because of the cluster" — eshkol is a cluster. The valley was called Cluster Valley after what the scouts cut there, a single bunch of grapes that took two men and a pole to carry.

  • v32 "a land that devours those who live in it" — the land they were sent to see as flowing with milk and honey (v27) they report as a land that eats. The same scouts brought back the fruit that proved the first report.

  • v33 "the Nephilim" — the word of Genesis 6:4, the Nephilim were in the earth in those days, and the word occurs only there and here. The clause the sons of Anak are from the Nephilim explains the name for the reader. The Greek has only we saw the giants, and not that clause.

  • v33 "and so we were in theirs" — the scouts report how they looked to the giants, which they had no way of knowing.

speech.text: Numbers 13
One Man from Each Tribe
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Send men to scout out the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the sons of Israel. You shall send one man from each tribe of their fathers, every one a chief among them."
So Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran at the command of the LORD, all of them men who were heads of the sons of Israel.
These were their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;
from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori;
from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;
from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;
from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;
from the tribe of Joseph, that is, from the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi;
from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;
from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;
from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;
from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.
These are the names of the men Moses sent to scout out the land. Moses called Hoshea son of Nun Joshua.
What to Look For
So Moses sent them to scout out the land of Canaan, and said to them, "Go up this way into the Negev, and go up into the hill country,
and see what the land is like, and whether the people who live in it are strong or weak, few or many,
and whether the land they live in is good or bad, and whether the cities they live in are open camps or fortified,
and whether the land is rich or poor, and whether there are trees in it or not. Be brave, and bring back some of the fruit of the land." Now it was the season of the first ripe grapes.
Forty Days
So they went up and scouted out the land from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, near Lebo-hamath.
They went up into the Negev, and he came to Hebron. Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai, the descendants of Anak, were there. Now Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.
They came to the valley of Eshcol, and cut down from there a branch with a single cluster of grapes, and they carried it on a pole between two of them, with some of the pomegranates and the figs.
That place was called the valley of Eshcol because of the cluster that the sons of Israel cut down there.
They came back from scouting out the land at the end of forty days.
The Report

They came to Moses and Aaron and to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel in the wilderness of Paran, at Kadesh. They brought back word to them and to the whole congregation, and showed them the fruit of the land.
They told him, "We came to the land where you sent us, and it does flow with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
But the people who live in the land are strong, and the cities are fortified and very large. We saw the descendants of Anak there too.
The Amalekites live in the land of the Negev; the Hittites, the Jebusites and the Amorites live in the hill country; and the Canaanites live by the sea and along the Jordan."
Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said, "We must go up at once and take possession of it, because we can surely overcome it."
But the men who had gone up with him said, "We cannot go up against the people, because they are stronger than we are."

They spread among the sons of Israel a bad report of the land they had scouted, saying, "The land we passed through to scout it out is a land that devours those who live in it, and all the people we saw in it are men of great size.
There we saw the Nephilim — the sons of Anak are from the Nephilim — and we were like grasshoppers in our own eyes, and so we were in theirs."

chapters.title: Forty Years for Forty Days
chapters.html:
Numbers 14

Let Us Go Back to Egypt

1The whole congregation raised their voices and cried out, and the people wept that night.

2All the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and against Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them, "If only we had died in the land of Egypt, or in this wilderness, if only we had died!

3Why is the LORD bringing us into this land to fall by the sword? Our wives and our little ones will become plunder. Would it not be better for us to go back to Egypt?"

4They said to one another, "Let us appoint a leader and go back to Egypt."

5Then Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before the whole assembly of the congregation of the sons of Israel.

6Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had scouted out the land, tore their clothes,

7and said to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, "The land we passed through to scout it out is a very, very good land.

8If the LORD delights in us, He will bring us into this land and give it to us, a land that flows with milk and honey.

9Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not fear the people of the land, for they are bread for us. Their shade has turned away from them, and the LORD is with us. Do not fear them."

10But the whole congregation said to stone them. The glory of the LORD appeared at the tent of meeting to all the sons of Israel.

Moses Pleads

11The LORD said to Moses, "How long will this people despise Me? How long will they not trust Me, in spite of all the signs I have done among them?

12I will strike them with pestilence and disinherit them, and I will make you into a nation greater and mightier than they are."

13But Moses said to the LORD, "Then the Egyptians will hear of it, for by Your power You brought this people up from among them,

14and they will tell the people who live in this land. They have heard that You, LORD, are among this people, that You, LORD, are seen eye to eye, that Your cloud stands over them, and that You go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and in a pillar of fire by night.

15If You put this people to death as one man, the nations who have heard Your fame will say,

16'It was because the LORD was not able to bring this people into the land He swore to give them that He slaughtered them in the wilderness.'

17So now, let the power of the Lord be great, as You have spoken, saying,

18'The LORD is slow to anger and abundant in loyal love, carrying guilt and rebellion, and not leaving it unpunished, calling the guilt of fathers to account on sons, on the third and on the fourth generation.'

19Please forgive the guilt of this people according to the greatness of Your loyal love, just as You have carried this people from Egypt until now."

20The LORD said, "I have forgiven, as you asked.

21But as I live, and as all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the LORD,

22none of the men who have seen My glory and My signs that I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and yet have tested Me these ten times and have not listened to My voice,

23shall see the land that I swore to their fathers. None of those who despised Me shall see it.

24But My servant Caleb, because there is a different spirit in him and he has followed Me fully — I will bring him into the land where he went, and his offspring shall possess it.

25Now the Amalekites and the Canaanites live in the valley. Tomorrow turn and set out into the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Reeds."

The Sentence

26The LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

27"How long shall this evil congregation go on grumbling against Me? I have heard the grumblings of the sons of Israel against Me.

28Say to them: As I live, declares the LORD, I will do to you exactly what you have said in My hearing.

29In this wilderness your bodies shall fall — all of you who were counted in your full number from twenty years old and upward, who have grumbled against Me.

30Not one of you shall come into the land where I raised My hand to settle you, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

31But your little ones, who you said would become plunder, I will bring in, and they shall know the land you have rejected.

32But as for you, your bodies shall fall in this wilderness.

33Your sons shall be shepherds in the wilderness forty years, and shall carry your unfaithfulness until the last of your bodies lies in the wilderness.

34By the number of the days you scouted out the land, forty days — a year for each day — you shall carry your guilt forty years, and you shall know what it is to have Me against you.

35I, the LORD, have spoken. I will surely do this to all this evil congregation that has gathered together against Me. In this wilderness they shall come to an end, and there they shall die."

36The men whom Moses sent to scout out the land, who came back and made the whole congregation grumble against him by spreading a bad report about the land —

37those men who spread the bad report about the land died by the plague before the LORD.

38But Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh remained alive, of the men who went to scout out the land.

Too Late

39Moses told these words to all the sons of Israel, and the people mourned greatly.

40They rose early in the morning and went up toward the top of the mountain, saying, "Here we are. We will go up to the place the LORD has spoken of, for we have sinned."

41But Moses said, "Why are you going against the command of the LORD? It will not succeed.

42Do not go up, for the LORD is not among you, or you will be struck down before your enemies.

43For the Amalekites and the Canaanites are there ahead of you, and you will fall by the sword. Because you have turned back from following the LORD, the LORD will not be with you."

44But they presumed to go up toward the top of the mountain, while neither the ark of the covenant of the LORD nor Moses moved out of the camp.

45Then the Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down and struck them and beat them down as far as Hormah.

Notes

  • v4 "Let us appoint a leader and go back to Egypt" — nittenah rosh, let us give ourselves a head. The people who were brought out of Egypt propose to choose their own leader and undo the Exodus. Nehemiah recalls this line in his prayer: they appointed a leader to return to their slavery (Nehemiah 9:17).

  • v9 "they are bread for us… their shade has turned away from them" — two pictures. The people of the land will be eaten up like bread, the answer to the scouts' a land that devours those who live in it (13:32). And their shade, their protection, as shade protects in desert heat, has left them.

  • vv17–18 "as You have spoken, saying" — Moses quotes God's own words from Exodus 34:6–7 back to Him, the words spoken when God passed before him on the mountain. He quotes them as the ground of his plea, and leaves some out: merciful and gracious, and truth, keeping loyal love for thousands.

  • v22 "these ten times" — zeh eser pe'amim. It may be a round number, again and again, or a count of the tests since the sea. The text does not list them.

  • v24 "a different spirit… he has followed Me fully" — va-yemalle acharai, literally he filled up after Me: he followed all the way. Joshua is named with Caleb in v30 and v38; here Caleb alone is singled out.

  • v33 "shall carry your unfaithfulness" — zenutekhem, from zanah, the word for prostitution that the Bible uses for unfaithfulness to God. The children bear the cost of it for forty years.

  • v34 "a year for each day" — yom la-shanah yom la-shanah, a day for the year, a day for the year. Forty days of looking at the land become forty years of not entering it.

  • v44 "they presumed" — va-ya'pilu, from the root of Habakkuk's here is one who is puffed up; his soul is not upright in him, but the righteous shall live by his faith (Habakkuk 2:4). They went up without the ark and without Moses.

  • v45 "as far as Hormah" — ha-chormah, from charam, to devote to destruction, the root of cherem, devoted (Leviticus 27:28). The place of their defeat bears the name of destruction.
